question.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 0 \\ -2 & 5 & 0 \\ 2 & -1 & 4\end{aligned}],\,J=[\begin{aligned}3 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 4\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrices above. Given that $A=PJ{P}^{-1}$ is a Jordan canonical decomposition of $A,$ which of the following could be the first column of the matrix $P?$

$$
x=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ -1\end{aligned}],\,y=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,z=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]
$$
question.worked_solution:
First, notice that the Jordan matrix $J$ may be written as a composition of Jordan blocks, as follows:

$$
J={J}_{2}(3)\,⊕\,{J}_{1}(4)
$$

So, we have

- one $2\times 2$ Jordan block corresponding to $\lambda =3,$ and

- one $1\times 1$ Jordan block corresponding to $\lambda =4.$

Therefore, the columns of $P$ form the following chains: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{J}_{2}(3) & : & {v}_{2}\overset{A-3I\,}{\to }{v}_{1}\overset{A-3I\,}{\to }0 &  \\ {J}_{1}(4) & : & {v}_{3}\overset{A-4I\,}{\to }0 & \end{aligned}
$$

As a result, the first column of $P$ is an eigenvector corresponding to $\lambda =3.$ 

Now, computing $A-3I,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}A-3I & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 0 \\ -2 & 5 & 0 \\ 2 & -1 & 4\end{aligned}]-3[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 2 & 0 \\ -2 & 2 & 0 \\ 2 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Among the given vectors, only 
$y$
is an eigenvector of $A,$ since

$$
(A-3I)y=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 2 & 0 \\ -2 & 2 & 0 \\ 2 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}],
$$

and we can write

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\overset{A-3I\,}{\to }0.\end{aligned}
$$

The other vectors do not satisfy this condition.
